newsitem.title: TURKEY: Pumping of Iraqi oil still not begun - Turkish TV.
newsitem.headline: Pumping of Iraqi oil still not begun - Turkish TV.

text.p: Turkish state television said on Tuesday that the planned pumping of Iraqi oil from Kirkuk in Iraq to Turkey under the U.N. oil-for-food deal had still not begun because of a technical fault.

"Iraq's process of pumping oil in the Kirkuk-Yumurtalik pipeline has still not started because of a fault in Kirkuk," TRT televison said in a news broadcast without stating its source. Turkish oil officials were not available for comment.
The official Iraqi News Agency reported earlier that President Saddam Hussein had pressed the button to resume Iraqi oil exports to world markets after a six-year break because of U.N. sanctions.
"But the station has not gone on line because of an electrical fault at Kirkuk," TRT said.

An official from the Turkish pipeline company Botas was quoted earlier by Turkey's Anatolian news agency as saying that the pumping of oil from Kirkuk to Yumurtalik terminal, at the coastal town of Ceyhan, would be delayed by one to two hours after the expected pumping time.
Turkish state refiner Tupras said it had signed a contract to buy 75,000 bpd of Iraqi oil and was expecting to begin loading it onto a tanker on December 13-14.

The United Nations gave Iraq clearance on Monday to start resuming limited exports of oil under an oil-for-food deal to relieve suffering of Iraqis who have been under economic sanctions imposed after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in 1990.

Under the U.N. plan, concluded in May but delayed by disputes over implementation, Iraq will be able to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian goods.
